items.title: Why the Bus Stop Moved
items.topic: a town moving a bus stop to improve safety near a busy crossing
items.action: compared walking routes before and after the proposed change
items.benefit: riders could wait farther from turning traffic and see approaching buses clearly
items.challenge: older riders worried that the new stop added several minutes of walking
items.lesson: a safer design should consider both traffic risk and the daily effort required from users
items.detail: the town added a bench and changed the crossing signal after receiving comments
items.reflection: Sofia learned that a good public decision may need several small adjustments rather than one perfect answer
items.titleJa: なぜバス停は移動したのか
items.topicJa: 交通安全のためのバス停移設
items.benefitJa: 右左折車から離れ見通しのよい場所で待てること
items.challengeJa: 高齢の利用者には歩く距離が増えること
items.lessonJa: 安全性だけでなく利用者の日々の負担も考える必要がある

items.title: A School Garden after Summer
items.topic: students restoring a school garden after a hot summer
items.action: recorded which plants survived and where the soil stayed moist
items.benefit: the class could redesign the garden using evidence from the previous season
items.challenge: students disagreed about whether to grow vegetables or native flowers
items.lesson: past results can guide a new plan while still leaving room for different goals
items.detail: half the beds were assigned to food plants and half to flowers for insects
items.reflection: Daniel saw that compromise worked better when each side could test its idea
items.topicJa: 猛暑後の学校菜園の立て直し
items.benefitJa: 前の季節の記録を次の設計に生かせること
items.challengeJa: 野菜と在来花のどちらを育てるか意見が分かれたこと
items.lessonJa: 過去の結果を使いながら複数の目標を試す余地を残せる

items.title: The Repair Café Experiment
items.topic: a monthly event where residents try to repair household objects
items.action: observed volunteers fixing lamps, toys, and small appliances
items.benefit: people saved money and learned why everyday objects stopped working
items.challenge: some visitors expected every broken item to be repaired immediately
items.lesson: repair programs need clear limits because learning and diagnosis can still be valuable when a fix is impossible
items.detail: volunteers began using cards that explained whether an item was repaired, partly repaired, or unsafe
items.reflection: Hana realized that success could mean understanding a problem, not only making an object work again
items.topicJa: 住民が生活用品の修理を試す月例会
items.benefitJa: 節約しながら故障の仕組みも学べること
items.challengeJa: すべてその場で直ると期待する人がいたこと
items.lessonJa: 修理できなくても診断や学びに価値があるため限界を明確にする必要がある

items.title: Counting Birds before Building
items.topic: students surveying birds before a wetland path was improved
items.action: visited at different times and recorded species near the planned route
items.benefit: planners gained local observations that could reduce disturbance
items.challenge: bird numbers changed with weather and time, making simple comparisons difficult
items.lesson: environmental observations become more useful when repeated under different conditions
items.detail: the final path avoided one nesting area and used a raised boardwalk
items.reflection: Owen learned that one visit can suggest a pattern but rarely proves it
items.topicJa: 湿地の遊歩道整備前に行う鳥類調査
items.benefitJa: 地域の観察記録を工事による影響の軽減に使えること
items.challengeJa: 天候や時間で鳥の数が変わり単純比較が難しいこと
items.lessonJa: 異なる条件で観察を繰り返すほど環境データは役立つ
